Builders for expressions

handle side effects of parent pointers, Sg_File_Info, lvalue etc.

Expressions are usually built using bottomup approach, i.e. buiding operands first, then the expression operating on the operands. It is also possible to build expressions with NULL operands or empty values first, then set them afterwards.

  • Value string is not included in the argument list for simplicty. It can be set afterwards using set_valueString()
  • Expression builders are organized roughtly in the order of class hierarchy list of ROSE Web Reference
  • default values for arguments are provided to support top-down construction. Should use SageInterface::setOperand(),setLhsOperand(), setRhsOperand() etc to set operands and handle side effects.

    SgAsmOp, SgAsteriskShapeExp, SgValueExp, SgEnumVal, SgThrowOp,

Builders for statements

AST high level builders for SgStatement, explicit scope parameters are allowed for flexibility. Please use SageInterface::appendStatement(), prependStatement(), and insertStatement() to attach the newly built statements into an AST tree. Calling member functions like SgScopeStatement::prepend_statement() or using container functions such as pushback() is discouraged since they don't handle many side effects for symbol tables, source file information, scope and parent pointers etc.

Untyped IR Node Build Interfaces

Build function for ROSE AST's in terms of Untyped IR nodes.

The ROSE Untyped IR nodes can be a starting place for defining the new language frontend, these IR nodes address the interface from an external language parser and the construction of the ROSE Untyped AST. Later iterations on the ROSE Untyped AST can be used to translate (or construct) a proper ROSE AST in terms of non-untyped IR nodes.

All untyped IR nodes have been removed and this interface removed. Ultimately it proved easier to construct regular IR nodes from the Jovial parser. Using the untyped system just led to an unnecessary step and wasted effort.

Scope stack interfaces

a global data structure to store current scope and parent scopes.

Scope stack is provided as an alternative to manually passing scope parameters to builder functions. It is not required to be used. Please use the recommendeded operation functions for maintaining the scope stack. Don't use raw container access functions to ScopeStack. e.g. avoid ScopeStack.push_back(), using pushScopeStack() instead.

Todo
consider complex cases:
  • how many scope stacks to keep? one. examine only one transparently
  • regular: push a child scope of current scope, add symbols etc.
  • irregular: push an arbitrary scope temporarily, add some symbol, then pop
  • even push a chain of scopes
  • restore scopes

◆ appendTemplateArgumentsToName()

ROSE_DLL_API SgName SageBuilder::appendTemplateArgumentsToName ( const SgName & name,
const SgTemplateArgumentPtrList & templateArgumentsList )

DQ (7/27/2012): changed semantics from removing the template arguments in names to adding the template arguments to names.

Appends template arguments to a given name to create a fully qualified template instantiation name.

This function constructs a string representation of a template name including its arguments (e.g., "Name<Arg1, Arg2>"). It iterates through a list of template arguments and attempts to resolve them to their fully qualified names to prevent symbol collisions in the symbol table. For type arguments, it strips modifiers like pointers and references and retrieves the qualified name from the underlying declaration (class, typedef, enum, or non-real decl). For non-type arguments, it attempts to resolve variable references to their initialized names.

The implementation uses an SgUnparse_Info object configured for C++ language rules, specifically skipping class/enum definitions and using generated names for template arguments. It handles various argument types including type_argument, nontype_argument, and template_template_argument.

Parameters
nameThe base SgName representing the template identifier before the angle brackets.
templateArgumentsListA list of pointers to SgTemplateArgument objects representing the arguments to be appended within the angle brackets.
Returns
An SgName representing the template name with the appended, qualified template arguments.
Precondition
The name parameter must be a valid, non-null SgName.
The templateArgumentsList should contain valid SgTemplateArgument pointers.
Postcondition
The returned SgName contains the original name followed by "<" and the processed arguments, ending with ">" if the argument list was not empty.
Note
This function is sensitive to the formatting of separators (e.g., " , " vs ",").
The function performs type stripping on type arguments using a bitmask that removes modifiers, references, pointers, and array types.
The function uses include and define logic internally via the ROSE framework for unparsing.
If an argument type is argument_undefined, the function will call ROSE_ABORT.

◆ buildAbstractHandle()

AbstractHandle::abstract_handle * SageInterface::buildAbstractHandle ( SgNode * n)

Build an abstract handle from a SgNode.

Builds an abstract handle from a given SgNode.

This function facilitates the creation of an abstract handle associated with a specific SgNode. It implements a caching mechanism using a static map to ensure that an abstract handle is only created once for any given SgNode, thereby avoiding duplicated creation and maintaining a 1:1 mapping between nodes and handles. If the handle does not exist in the map, the function uses AbstractHandle::buildroseNode to create an abstract node and then wraps it in a new abstract handle.

Parameters
nA pointer to the SgNode from which the abstract handle is to be built.
Returns
A pointer to the AbstractHandle::abstract_handle associated with the input node.
Precondition
n must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If a new handle was created, it is stored in a static map for future retrieval.
Note
The function uses a static std::map to track existing handles, which means the mapping persists across multiple calls to this function during the lifetime of the program.
Warning
The use of a static map may lead to memory accumulation if SgNodes are frequently created and destroyed, as the map holds references to the SgNode pointers.

Build an aggregate initializer.

Builds an aggregate initializer expression.

This function constructs a new SgAggregateInitializer object representing an aggregate initialization in the ROSE AST. It initializes the object with the provided list of initializers and the target type. The function ensures that the parent-child relationship is established by setting the initializers' parent to the newly created initializer if the list is not NULL. Additionally, it configures the initializer to require explicit braces and synchronizes the source position for transformation purposes.

Parameters
initializersA pointer to an SgExprListExp containing the expressions to be used as initializers. Can be NULL.
typeA pointer to the SgType representing the type of the aggregate being initialized. Can be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgAggregateInitializer object.
Precondition
The initializers and type pointers should be valid ROSE AST nodes if not NULL.
Postcondition
A new SgAggregateInitializer is allocated on the heap. If initializers is not NULL, its parent is set to the returned SgAggregateInitializer.
Note
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to ensure the successful allocation of the result object.

◆ buildBracedInitializer()

ROSE_DLL_API SgBracedInitializer * SageBuilder::buildBracedInitializer ( SgExprListExp * initializers,
SgType * expression_type )

Build an braced initializer.

Constructs a new SgBracedInitializer object from a list of initializers and a type.

This function instantiates an SgBrachedInitializer node within the ROSE AST. It encapsulates a list of expressions (initializers) under a single braced initializer node of a specified type. The function handles the necessary parent-child relationship setup by assigning the newly created initializer node as the parent of the initializers list, provided the list is not null. It also ensures that source position information is propagated to the new node.

Parameters
initializersA pointer to an SgExprListExp containing the expressions to be included in the braced initializer list. Can be NULL.
expression_typeA pointer to the SgType representing the type of the braced initializer.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgBracedInitializer object.
Precondition
expression_type should be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgType object.
Postcondition
If initializers is not NULL, the parent of the initializers object is set to the returned SgBracedInitializer.
The returned SgBracedInitializer node will have its source position synchronized via setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to ensure the successful allocation of the SgBracedInitializer.

It handles the basic setup of the initializer, including setting the parent pointer of the initializers list if it is not null. The source position of the resulting object is explicitly set to null, making this a "no-file-info" (nfi) variant of the builder.

Parameters
initializersA pointer to an SgExprListExp containing the expressions to be included in the braced initializer. Can be NULL.

Precondition
The expression_type parameter should be a valid pointer to an SgType object.
Postcondition
The returned SgBracedInitializer has its source position set to null. If initializers is not NULL, its parent is set to the returned result.
Note
This function is part of the SageBuilder utility and is intended for internal AST construction where precise source location tracking is not required.

◆ buildClassDefinition()

ROSE_DLL_API SgClassDefinition * SageBuilder::buildClassDefinition ( SgClassDeclaration * d,
bool buildTemplateInstantiation )

Build a class definition scope statement.

Constructs a new SgClassDefinition or SgTemplateInstantiationDefn object.

This function initializes a class definition object based on the provided declaration. It determines whether to create a standard SgClassDefinition or a template instantiation (SgTemplateInstantiationDefn) based on the buildTemplateInstantiation flag and the nature of the input declaration. The function also configures case-insensitivity settings based on the current language semantics and ensures the resulting object has a valid source position.

Parameters
dA pointer to an SgClassDeclaration to be used as the basis for the new definition. If this is NULL, an empty definition is created.
buildTemplateInstantiationA boolean flag indicating whether the function should attempt to build a template instantiation.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgClassDefinition or SgTemplateInstantiationDefn object.
Precondition
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true and d is not NULL, d must be a valid template instantiation declaration (verified via isSgTemplateInstantiationDecl).
Postcondition
The returned object is guaranteed to be non-NULL due to the ROSE_ASSERT(result) check.
Note
The function handles case-insensitivity by checking SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive().
If d is NULL, the function creates a default-constructed definition.

Build a class definition scope statement.

Constructs a class definition or template instantiation object based on a declaration.

This function creates an instance of either SgClassDefinition or SgTemplateInstantiationDefn. The logic branches based on whether a source declaration is provided and whether the caller intends to build a template instantiation. If a declaration is provided, the function verifies the validity of the template instantiation via a ROSE_ASSERT. The function also configures the case-sensitivity of the resulting object based on the current language settings via SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive().

Parameters
dA pointer to an SgClassDeclaration from which to derive the definition. If NULL, a new, empty definition is created.
buildTemplateInstantiationA boolean flag indicating whether to create a template instantiation object instead of a standard class definition.

Precondition
If buildTemplateInstantiation is true and d is not NULL, d must be a valid template instantiation declaration (verifiable via isSgTemplateInstantiationDecl).
Postcondition
The returned object will have its case-sensitivity set according to the current language settings and its source position will be initialized to NULL.
Note
This function includes a safety check to prevent segmentation faults by verifying that d is not NULL before attempting to access its properties.

Constructs a new SgComplexVal object from real and imaginary components.

This function instantiates a new SgComplexVal node in the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It initializes the complex value using the provided real and imaginary expression nodes. The function also handles the maintenance of the AST hierarchy by updating the parent pointers of the input expression nodes to point to the newly created complex value node. The type of the complex value is derived from the type of the imaginary component.

Parameters

A pointer to the newly created SgComplexVal object.
Precondition
imaginary_value must not be NULL to allow for type extraction.
Postcondition
If real_value or imaginary_value are not NULL, their parent pointer will be set to the returned SgComplexVal.
The returned SgComplex and its children will have a consistent source position.
Note
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify the successful allocation of the result and to ensure that the parent-child relationship is correctly established.

This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate that imaginary_value is not NULL and that the resulting SgComplexVal was successfully allocated.

Constructs a new conditional expression node in the Sg tree.

This function instantiates a new SgConditionalExp object representing a ternary-style conditional operation. It establishes the structural relationship between the conditional expression and its constituent components (the test condition, the true branch, and the false branch) by updating the parent pointers of each provided expression. Additionally, it ensures that the newly created node inherits a unified source position for transformation consistency.

Parameters
testThe expression representing the condition to be evaluated.
aThe expression to be returned if the test evaluates to true.
bThe expression to be returned if the test evaluates to false.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgConditionalExp node.
Precondition
The provided expressions (test, a, b) should ideally not already have a parent that is part of a different branch of the Sg tree to avoid structural inconsistencies.
Postcondition
The returned SgConditionalExp node's parent pointers are set to the newly created node for all non-null input expressions.
Note
This function uses new to allocate the SgConditionalExp on the heap; the caller or the tree management system is responsible for memory deallocation.

◆ buildConditionalExp_nfi()

SgConditionalExp * SageBuilder::buildConditionalExp_nfi ( SgExpression * test,
SgExpression * a,
SgExpression * b,
SgType * t )

Constructs a conditional expression node with null-friendly handling for its components.

This function instantiates a new SgConditionalExp object and establishes the necessary structural relationships within the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It performs parent-child linking for the test condition and the two branches (a and b). If the branches are non-null, it also invokes markLhsValues to ensure that any left-hand side values within those expressions are correctly flagged for analysis. The source position of the resulting node is initialized to null.

Parameters
testThe expression representing the condition to be evaluated.
aThe expression to be returned if the test evaluates to true.
bThe expression to be returned if the test evaluates to false.
tThe resulting type of the conditional expression.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgConditionalExp node.
Precondition
The provided SgExpression pointers (test, a, b) should be valid or null.
Postcondition
The returned SgConditionalExp node will have its parent pointers updated to point to itself for all non-null input expressions.
Note
This function is specifically designed to handle cases where some components of the conditional expression might be null (nfi suffix).

The function links the provided body and condition statements to the result object and establishes the necessary parent-child relationships.

The result object's condition is set to the provided condition statement.
The parent of the body statement is set to the result object.
The parent of the condition statement is set to the result object.
The source position of the result object is set to null.
Note
This function relies on ASSERT macros to validate the integrity of the AST construction process and ensure that the resulting tree structure is valid.

◆ buildEmptyDeclaration()

ROSE_DLL_API SgEmptyDeclaration * SageBuilder::buildEmptyDeclaration ( )

Build an empty declaration (useful for adding precission to comments and CPP handling under token-based unparsing).

Creates and initializes a new empty declaration object.

This function instantiates an SgEmptyDeclaration object and performs the necessary initialization to make it a valid, self-referencing node within the AST. It sets the defining and first non-defining declarations to point to itself, establishes the source position based on the current transformation context, and assigns the current top scope as its parent. This is particularly useful for maintaining structural integrity during token-based unparsing, such as when adding precision information to comments or handling CPP directives.

Returns
A pointer to the newly created and initialized SgEmptyDeclaration object.
Precondition
The top scope stack must be accessible via topScopeStack().
Postcondition
A new SgEmptyDeclaration is allocated on the heap. The object's parent is set to the current top scope stack, and its defining/non-defining declaration pointers are set to itself.
Note
The parent assignment is performed with the understanding that certain declaration types (like class or enum declarations) may not always have a parent set due to potential non-autonomous nature.

◆ buildFortranImplicitType()

SgType * SageBuilder::buildFortranImplicitType ( SgName sg_name)

Determines the implicit type of a variable based on Fortran naming conventions.

Put Fortran-specific builders here.

Build a type based on Fortran's implicit typing rules. Currently this interface does not take into account possible implicit statements that change the rules.

This function implements the standard Fortran implicit typing rules. The type assigned to a variable is determined by the first character of its name. Specifically, variables starting with letters A through H or O through Z are assigned a floating-point type, while variables starting with letters I through N are assigned an integer type.

Parameters
sg_nameThe name of the variable used to determine the implicit type.
Returns
A pointer to the SgType representing the determined implicit type (either a float or integer type). Returns NULL if the type could not be constructed.
Precondition
The first character of the provided sg_name must be a lowercase or uppercase alphabetic character (a-z or A-Z).
Postcondition
The returned SgType pointer will not be NULL, provided the input name satisfies the precondition.
Note
The implementation uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate that the first character of the name is within the alphabetic range.

Build a function call expression,it will automatically search for function symbols internally to build a right function reference etc. It tolerates the lack of the function symbol to support generating calls to library functions whose headers have not yet been inserted.

This function automates the creation of an SgFunctionCallExp by synthesizing the necessary underlying components, including the function type, parameter type list, and function reference. It handles the initialization of the scope and parameter list if they are provided as null. The implementation follows a bottom-up construction approach: first determining the parameter types, then the function type, then the function reference, and finally the call expression itself. It also ensures that the parent-child relationship is maintained by setting the parent of the parameter list to the newly created call expression.

Precondition
The scope must be non-null, or the top scope stack must contain a valid scope.
Postcondition
A valid SgFunctionCallExp is returned, and its parameters' parent is set to the call expression.
Note
This function relies on internal builder methods such as buildExprListExp, buildFunctionParameterTypeList, buildFunctionType, and buildFunctionRefExp. It also updates the source position for the transformation using setOneSourcePositionForTransformation.

◆ buildFunctionCallExp() [3/3]

ROSE_DLL_API SgFunctionCallExp * SageBuilder::buildFunctionCallExp ( SgFunctionSymbol * sym,
SgExprListExp * parameters )

Build a function call expression.

Constructs an expression representing a function call.

This function creates a new SgFunctionCallExp object based on a provided function symbol and a list of parameters. The implementation distinguishes between standard function calls and member function calls. If the provided symbol is identified as an SgMemberFunctionSymbol, the function builds an SgMemberFunctionRefExp to preserve the semantics of member access, which is critical for the analysis of object-oriented languages like C++ and Java. For non-member functions, it builds an SgFunctionRefExp. The function also handles the initialization of an empty parameter list if none is provided.

Parameters
symA pointer to the SgFunctionSymbol representing the function to be called. Must not be NULL.
parametersA pointer to an SgExprListExp containing the arguments for the function call. If NULL, a new empty expression list will be created.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgFunctionCallExp object.
Precondition
sym must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If parameters was NULL, a new SgExprListExp is allocated and linked to the function call.
The returned SgFunctionCallExp has its parent-child relationships established with the function reference and the parameter list.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate that sym and the resulting parameters are not NULL.
The function preserves support for member functions as SgMemberFunctionRefExp to prevent the lowering of member calls to simple function calls, which would impede object-oriented analysis.

Build SgFunctionRefExp based on a C++ function's name and function type. It will lookup symbol table internally starting from scope. A hidden prototype will be created internally to introduce a new function symbol if the function symbol cannot be found.

Constructs a function reference expression for a given function name and type.

This function creates an SgFunctionRefExp representing a reference to a function. It attempts to locate the function symbol within the provided scope or parent scopes. If the function symbol cannot be found, the function attempts to create a new function declaration in the global scope (assuming it is not a member function) to serve as a prototype. This is particularly useful in scenarios where function calls are encountered before their corresponding prototypes are defined.

If scope is provided, it must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If the function symbol is not found and the function is not a member function, a new function declaration is inserted into the global scope.
The returned SgFunctionRefExp is initialized with the appropriate symbol and type.
Note
This implementation assumes that only regular (non-member) functions can be automatically declared in the global scope when a symbol is missing.
The function handles language-specific declaration differences for Fortran or Jovial using SgProcedureHeaderStatement versus SgFunctionDeclaration.

◆ buildLabelStatement()

ROSE_DLL_API SgLabelStatement * SageBuilder::buildLabelStatement ( const SgName & name,
SgStatement * stmt = NULL,
SgScopeStatement * scope = NULL )

Build a label statement, name is the label's name. Handling label symbol and scope internally.

Constructs a new SgLabelStatement object representing a labeled statement.

Note that the scope of a label statement is special. It is SgFunctionDefinition, not the closest scope statement such as SgBasicBlock.

This function creates an instance of SgLabelStatement associated with a specific name. It handles the initialization of the label statement, including setting the source position and establishing the parent-child relationship between the label and the provided statement if one is present. If a scope is provided, the function performs label fixing (via fixLabelStatement) provided the language is not Fortran. For Fortran, the label statement is treated as a mechanism for CONTINUE statements and does not inherently associate with a Label symbol at this stage.

Parameters
nameThe SgName representing the identifier for the label.
stmtThe SgStatement that the label points to. If NULL, the label is created without an associated statement.
scopeThe SgScopeStatement within which the label is defined. If NULL, the function retrieves the top of the current scope stack.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgLabelStatement object.
Precondition
The name parameter must be a valid SgName.
Postcondition
If stmt is not NULL, stmt's parent is set to the newly created labelstmt.
If the language is not Fortran and scope is provided, the label statement is processed via fixLabelStatement.
Note
The parent of the label statement itself is not set within this function; this operation is delayed until methods like append_statement() are called.
In Fortran, SgLabelStatement is used for CONTINUE statements and does not have an inherent association with a Label symbol here; symbol association is handled by SageInterface::setNumericalLabel.

◆ buildLambdaExp()

ROSE_DLL_API SgLambdaExp * SageBuilder::buildLambdaExp ( SgLambdaCaptureList * lambda_capture_list,
SgClassDeclaration * lambda_closure_class,
SgFunctionDeclaration * lambda_function )

DQ (9/3/2014): Adding support for C++11 Lambda expressions.

Constructs a new SgLambdaExp node and establishes its structural relationships.

This function instantiates an SgLambdaExp object using the provided capture list, closure class, and function declaration. It is responsible for maintaining the integrity of the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) by setting the parent pointers for the constituent components (capture list, closure class, and function declaration) to the newly created lambda expression. The function also updates the source position of the expression.

Parameters
lambda_capture_listA pointer to the SgLambdaCaptureList representing the variables captured by the lambda. Can be NULL.
lambda_closure_classA pointer to the SgClassDeclaration representing the class generated to handle the lambda closure. Can be NULL.
lambda_functionA pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration representing the actual function body/signature of the lambda. Can be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgLambdaExp object.
Precondition
The provided pointers (lambda_capture_list, lambda_closure_class, lambda_function) should be valid AST nodes if they are not NULL.
Postcondition
The returned SgLambdaExp node will have its source position set. If the input components are not NULL, their parent pointer will be set to the new SgLambdaExp node.
Note
The implementation contains a if 1 block that unconditionally sets the parent of lambda_function to the expr, bypassing the alternative logic that would otherwise attempt to link it to the lambda_closure_class.
Warning
If lambda_function is not NULL, its parent is set to expr regardless of whether lambda_closure_class is NULL.

Parameters: className: template class name, e.g. vector objectExpression: the variable reference expression to an object of template class instantiation: vector<int> var1; functionName: member function name: size params: function parameter list scope: the scope this function call expression will be inserted into. Credit to Peter's previous work at: projects/MatlabTranslation/src/transformations/MatlabSimpleTransformer.cc

This function automates the creation of a member function call expression by resolving the class symbol and the function symbol within the provided scope. It performs a lookup of the class symbol in the parent scopes of the provided scope, retrieves the class definition, and then searches for the function symbol within that class definition. Once the function symbol is identified, it builds a member function reference expression and wraps it into a function call expression using the provided object expression and parameters.

Parameters
classNameThe name of the class containing the member function to be called.
objectExpressionThe expression representing the object on which the member function is called.
functionNameThe name of the member function to be called.
paramsAn expression list containing the arguments to be passed to the member function.
scopeThe scope within which the class and function lookups should be performed.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgFunctionCallExp representing the member function call.
Precondition
The className must correspond to a valid class symbol resolvable within the provided scope.
The functionName must correspond to a valid member function symbol within the resolved class definition.
The class symbol must have a valid defining declaration and definition.
Postcondition
Returns a valid SgFunctionCallExp if all lookups and assertions succeed.
Warning
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the existence of the class symbol, class declaration, class definition, and function symbol. If any of these lookups fail, the program will abort.
Note
The implementation relies on SageInterface::lookupClassSymbolInParentScopes and lookupFunctionSymbolInParentScopes for symbol resolution.

◆ buildMemberFunctionType() [1/2]

ROSE_DLL_API SgMemberFunctionType * SageBuilder::buildMemberFunctionType ( SgType * return_type,
SgFunctionParameterTypeList * typeList,
SgScopeStatement * struct_name,
unsigned int mfunc_specifier )

Constructs or retrieves a member function type based on the provided signature and scope.

This function facilitates the creation of an SgMemberFunctionType. It first attempts to build a temporary version of the type to generate a mangled name. It then uses this mangled name to perform a lookup in the global function type table. If the type is found in the table, the temporary object is deleted and the existing instance is returned. This mechanism is designed to resolve subtle C++ specific issues related to the build interface and compatibility with newer EDG connections to ROSE.

The implementation identifies the underlying class or declaration scope from the provided struct_name, determines the appropriate class type, and then delegates the actual type construction to a refactored internal version of buildMemberFunctionType.

Parameters
return_typeThe return type of the member function. Must not be NULL.
typeListA list of parameters for the function. Can be NULL if the function has no parameters.
struct_nameThe scope statement (such as a class or struct definition) that contains the member function. Must not be NULL and must have a valid parent.
mfunc_specifierAn unsigned integer representing function specifiers (e.g., const, volatile, etc.).
Returns
A pointer to the constructed or retrieved SgMemberFunctionType.
Precondition
return_type != NULL
struct_name != NULL
struct_name->get_parent() != NULL
The struct_name must resolve to either an SgClassDefinition or an SgDeclarationScope.
Postcondition
The returned SgMemberFunctionType will be a valid object existing either as a newly created instance or a retrieved instance from the global function type table.
Note
If typeList is NULL, a warning is printed to the standard output.
The function relies on include and define logic within the ROSE framework for type checking and assertion handling.

DQ (8/19/2012): Refactored some of the code supporting construction of the SgMemberFunctionType.

Constructs or retrieves a member function type from the global function type table.

This function manages the creation and caching of SgMemberFunctionType objects. It first attempts to look up a mangled name in the global function type table. If the type does not exist, it constructs a new type by first creating an SgPartialFunctionType, populating it with the provided parameters, and then using SgMemberFunctionType::createType to finalize the type. The function ensures that the global type table remains consistent by inserting newly created types and reusing existing ones.

Parameters

typeListThe list of parameters for the member function.
classTypeThe class type to which this member function belongs.
mfunc_specifierAn unsigned integer representing the member function specifiers (e. if, ifdef, etc., are not used here, but specifiers like const or volatile are encoded here).
Returns
A pointer to the constructed or retrieved SgMemberFunctionType.
Precondition
typeList must not be NULL.
The global function type table must be accessible via SgNode::get_globalFunctionTypeTable().
Postcondition
If a new type is created, it is inserted into the global function type table.
The returned SgMemberFunctionType will have its argument list set to the provided typeList.
Note
This implementation uses a temporary SgPartialFunctionType to facilitate the creation of the SgMemberFunctionType and cleans up the temporary object after use.

Generates an assembly statement representing a multi-byte NOP instruction of a specific length.

DQ (4/30/2010): Added support for building nop statement using asm statement Building nop statement using asm statement

This function constructs an assembly statement object for NOP (No-Operation) instructions ranging from 1 to 9 bytes in length. It uses a predefined set of instruction strings (implemented via define directives) that represent various multi-byte NOP sequences, including both mnemonic-based instructions and raw byte sequences. The function maps the input integer n to the corresponding assembly string and wraps it into an SgAsmStmt object.

Parameters
nThe desired length of the NOP instruction in bytes. Supported values are integers from 1 to 9.
Returns
A pointer to an SgAsmStmt object containing the generated NOP instruction.
Precondition
n must be greater than 0.
Postcondition
Returns a valid SgAsmStmt pointer if n is between 1 and 9.
Warning
If n is greater than 9, the function will print an error message and trigger a ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program.
Note
The implementation relies on several define macros (e.g., NOP_1_BYTE_STRING) to store the assembly string representations.

Constructs a non-defining function declaration, supporting templates, member functions, and instantiations.

This function is responsible for creating and registering a function declaration (prototype) within the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It handles various types of declarations including standard functions, member functions, template functions, and template instantiations. The implementation performs symbol table lookups to either reuse existing symbols (for subsequent prototypes of the same function) or create new symbols and insert them into the provided scope. It also manages template arguments, template parameters, and storage modifiers (such as static). For Fortran, it specifically handles the distinction between subroutines and functions.

scopeThe scope in which the declaration is being built. If NULL, the top of the scope stack is used.

templateArgumentsListA list of template arguments, used if the function is a template instantiation.
templateParameterListA list of template parameters, used if the function is a template declaration.
smThe storage modifier (e.g., static) to be applied to the function declaration.

return_type must not be NULL.
paralist must not be NULL.
If the function is a template instantiation, templateArgumentsList must not be NULL.
Postcondition
A new or existing actualFunction node representing the non-defining declaration is returned.
The function symbol is inserted into the provided scope if it is a new declaration.
The function's parameter list is updated and source positions are set for the parameters.
Note
This function handles the complexity of template-based overloading by using template arguments during symbol table lookup while maintaining the base name for name generation.
For Fortran language support, the function distinguishes between subroutines and functions based on the return type.
The function handles the case where a symbol might be found in a different scope and ensures it is correctly inserted into the current scope if necessary.

! Same as buildClassTemplateType(), just better name ROSE_DLL_API SgClassType* buildTemplateClassType(SgTemplateClassDeclaration* template_decl, Rose_STL_Container<SgNode *>& template_args);

! Build an opaque type with a name, useful when a type's details are unknown during transformation, especially for a runtime library's internal type. Must provide scope here. /*! Some types are not known during translation but nevertheless are needed. For example, some internal types from a runtime library. This function creates an opaque type definition, which is particularly useful when the internal details of a type are unknown during a transformation process, such as when dealing with internal types in a runtime library. The function checks if a typedef symbol with the provided name already exists in the specified scope. If it does not, a new SgTypedefDeclaration is instantiated, initialized as an integer type, and inserted into the scope. The function also ensures the declaration is prepended to the scope and configured to be hidden from the unparser. If the symbol already exists, the existing type is retrieved.

A pointer to the SgType representing the opaque type (specifically an SgTypedefType).

The scope parameter must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If the type does not exist, a new SgTypedefDeclaration is added to the scope and the scope's statement list is updated.
Note
The implementation uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the existence of the scope and the successful creation of the type declaration and symbol.
The created type is configured to have its output unset in code generation via the Sg_File_Info object.

◆ buildOpaqueVarRefExp()

ROSE_DLL_API SgVarRefExp * SageBuilder::buildOpaqueVarRefExp ( const std::string & varName,
SgScopeStatement * scope = NULL )

Build a variable reference expression at scope to an opaque variable which has unknown information except for its name. Used when referring to an internal variable defined in some headers of runtime libraries.(The headers are not yet inserted into the file during translation). Similar to buildOpaqueType();.

Creates a variable reference expression for a variable that may or may not already exist in the scope.

It will declare a hidden int varName at the specified scope to cheat the AST consistence tests.

This function attempts to find a variable symbol with the given name within the provided scope or the top scope stack. If the symbol is found and is a variable symbol, it builds a reference expression for that existing symbol. If the symbol is not found, the function creates a "fake" variable declaration (an opaque declaration) within the specified scope using an integer type, and then builds a reference expression to this newly created symbol. This is useful for handling references to variables that are not explicitly declared in the current AST but are assumed to exist.

Parameters
nameThe string identifier of the variable to be referenced.
scopeThe scope in which to search for the variable. If this is NULL, the function defaults to using the top of the current scope stack via SageBuilder::topScopeStack().
Returns
A pointer to the constructed SgVarRefExp representing the variable reference. Returns NULL if the construction fails, though the function uses ROSE_ASSERT to ensure a valid scope is available.
Precondition
The scope parameter, if provided, must not be NULL. If scope is NULL, SageBuilder::topScopeStack() must return a non-NULL SgScopeStatement.
Postcondition
If the variable name exists in the scope, a reference to the existing symbol is returned. If the variable name does not exist, a new SgVariableDeclaration is added to the provided scope, and a reference to this new declaration is returned.
Note
This implementation uses lookupVariableSymbolInParentScopes to ensure the symbol found is specifically a variable symbol.
The function modifies the scope by adding a new variable declaration if the variable is not found.

parameter_list must not be null.

Note
This function relies on internal assertions to ensure the validity of the return type and parameter list.

◆ buildSourceFile() [1/2]

ROSE_DLL_API SgSourceFile * SageBuilder::buildSourceFile ( const std::string & inputFileName,
const std::string & outputFileName,
SgProject * project,
bool clear_globalScopeAcrossFiles = false )

Build a SgSourceFile node and attach it to SgProject.

Constructs an SgSourceFile object from an input file and maps it to an output file.

The input file will be loaded if exists, or an empty one will be generated from scratch transparently. Output file name is used to specify the output file name of unparsing. The final SgFile will be inserted to project automatically. If not provided, a new SgProject will be generated internally. Using SgFile->get_project() to retrieve it in this case.

This function handles the creation of a source file representation within a project. It invokes buildFile to parse the input file, then performs a secondary pass to handle token-based unparsing and attaches preprocessing information. The function also ensures that if the file being built is a duplicate of an existing file in the project, certain optimization flags are synchronized. Finally, it updates the source position information to reflect the output filename and resets the modified flag on the global scope to ensure consistency for subsequent token-stream mapping.

Parameters
inputFileNameThe path to the original source file to be read and parsed.
outputFileNameThe path to the target output file that the resulting SgSourceFile should represent.
projectA pointer to the SgProject containing the file list and global context.
clear_globalScopeAcrossFilesA boolean flag indicating whether the global scope should be cleared across files during the build process.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgSourceFile object.
Precondition
project must not be NULL.
The input file must be accessible for reading.
Postcondition
The returned SgSourceFile's global scope is guaranteed to have its modified flag set to false.
The source position information in the IR nodes is updated to match outputFileName.
Note
This function uses include and define logic implicitly through the secondary pass over the source file to ensure CPP directives and comments are correctly attached.
The function relies on the existence of buildFile and secondaryPassOverSourceFile to perform the heavy lifting of parsing and attribute attachment.

ROSE_DLL_API SgTypeString * SageBuilder::buildStringType ( SgExpression * stringLengthExpression)

Constructs an SgTypeString node based on a provided length expression.

This function creates a new SgTypeString object that represents a string type. The implementation utilizes the SgTypeString::createType factory method, which is capable of handling both literal values and complex expressions to define the string's length. This specific type implementation is tailored for Fortran compatibility, as Fortran requires explicit string length handling, whereas C/C++ typically treats strings as character arrays.

Parameters
stringLengthExpressionAn expression representing the length of the string. This can be a literal value or a more complex SgExpression.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgTypeString object.
Precondition
stringLengthExpression should be a valid SgExpression pointer.
Postcondition
Returns a non-null SgTypeString pointer, provided the internal creation mechanism succeeds.
Note
The current implementation reflects the grammatical differences between Fortran and C/C++. While C/C++ strings are often just arrays of char, this node is specifically used to support the Fortran-style string length requirements within the IR.

Builds a template class declaration and its associated non-defining declaration.

@fileoverview This file contains the implementation of the logic for the get_token_stream_from_config_file function.

Author
Your Name
Date
2023-10-27

This function is responsible for constructing the IR nodes for a template class declaration, including both the defining declaration (the implementation/template definition) and the non-defining declaration (the forward declaration). It handles the creation of the template name with and without template specialization arguments, manages the template parameter lists, and ensures that the symbol table is updated with the appropriate template class symbols. The function also handles the logic for reusing an existing defining declaration if a non-defining declaration is provided.

Parameters
XXX_nameThe name of the template class.
kindThe type of the class (e.g., class or struct).
scopeThe scope in which the declaration is being built. If NULL, the top scope stack is used.
nonDefiningDeclA pointer to an existing non-defining declaration to be used or updated. If NULL, a new non-defining declaration will be created.
templateParameterListA list of template parameters associated with the template class.
templateSpecializationArgumentListA list of template arguments used for template specialization.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created or reused SgTemplateClassDeclaration representing the defining declaration of the template class.
Precondition
scope must not be NULL (if NULL, it defaults to the top scope stack).
templateParameterList must not be NULL.
templateSpecialragumentList must not be NULL.
If nonDefiningDecl is not NULL, its first non-defining declaration must be itself.
Postcondition
The returned SgTemplateClassDeclaration is properly linked to its defining declaration.
The non-defining declaration is linked to the defining declaration.
The template parameters and template specialization arguments are correctly assigned to both declarations.
The symbol table in the provided scope is updated with the template class symbol.
Note
The function handles the distinction between the template name (without specialization arguments) and the specialized name (with specialization arguments).
The function uses include, define, and other preprocessor directives internally for debugging and conditional compilation.

ROSE_DLL_API SgVarRefExp * SageBuilder::buildVarRefExp ( const SgName & name,
SgScopeStatement * scope = NULL )

Build SgVarRefExp based on a variable's Sage name. It will lookup the name in the symbol table internally starting from scope. A variable name is unique so type can be inferred (double check this).

Creates a variable reference expression for a given name within a specific scope.

It is possible to build a reference to a variable with known name before the variable is declared, especially during bottomup construction of AST. In this case, SgTypeUnknown is used to indicate the variable reference needing postprocessing fix using fixVariableReferences() once the AST is complete and all variable declarations exist. But the side effect is that some get_type() operations may not recognize the unknown type before the fix. So far, I extended SgPointerDerefExp::get_type() and SgPntrArrRefExp::get_type() for SgTypeUnknown. There may be others needing the same extension.

This function attempts to locate a variable symbol associated with the provided name within the specified scope or the top-level scope if no scope is provided. If the symbol is found, it creates a variable reference expression pointing to that symbol. If the symbol is not found, the function creates a placeholder initialized name with an unknown type and a corresponding variable symbol, which is intended to be cleaned up during a subsequent post-processing phase.

Parameters
nameThe name of the variable to be referenced, encapsulated in an SgName object.
scopeThe scope in which to perform the lookup. If this is NULL, the function defaults to the top scope stack via SageBuilder::topScopeStack().
Returns
A pointer to a newly created SgVarRefExp representing the variable reference.
Precondition
The name parameter must be a valid SgName.
Postcondition
A new SgVarRefExp is allocated on the heap. If the symbol was not found in the provided scope, a new SgVariableSymbol is created and attached to the scope.
Note
This function uses lookupVariableSymbolInParentScopes to perform the symbol lookup. If the symbol is not found, the function creates a "fake" initialization name using SgTypeUnknown::createType().
The function relies on ROSE_ASSERT to ensure that the resulting varSymbol and varRef are not NULL.

◆ findAssociatedDeclarationInTargetAST()

ROSE_DLL_API SgDeclarationStatement * SageBuilder::findAssociatedDeclarationInTargetAST ( SgDeclarationStatement * snippet_declaration,

Finds the corresponding declaration in a target AST based on a snippet declaration.

This function traverses the scope hierarchy of a provided snippet declaration up to its global scope, and then traverses down through the scope hierarchy of a target AST scope to locate the matching declaration (such as a class, typedef, enum, or function) in the target AST. It is specifically designed to support code segregation by mapping declarations across different ASTs that do not share the same global scope.

Parameters
snippet_declarationA pointer to the declaration statement in the source snippet that needs to be matched in the target AST.
targetScopeA pointer to the scope statement in the target AST where the search for the associated declaration should begin.
Returns

Precondition
snippet_declaration and targetScope must not be NULL.
The snippet_declaration and targetScope must not share the same global scope.
All intermediate scopes between the snippet_declaration and the global scope must be named scopes.
Postcondition
The returned declaration, if not NULL, will have a name matching the snippet_declaration and will reside in a different global scope than the snippet.
Note
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the integrity of the AST traversal, including checks that the snippet and target scopes belong to different global scopes.
The implementation handles various declaration types including V_SgClassDeclaration, V_SgTypedefDeclaration, V_SgEnumDeclaration, V_SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration, V_SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration, V_SgMemberFunctionDeclaration, and V_SgFunctionDeclaration.
Unnamed enum declarations are not supported and will trigger an assertion failure.

◆ findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST()

ROSE_DLL_API SgSymbol * SageBuilder::findAssociatedSymbolInTargetAST ( SgDeclarationStatement * snippet_declaration,
SgScopeStatement * targetScope )

Finds the corresponding symbol in a target AST that matches a declaration from a snippet AST.

This function performs a cross-AST symbol lookup. It begins by traversing upwards from the provided snippet declaration to the global scope, recording the sequence of scopes encountered. It then performs a reverse traversal of this scope list, starting from the global scope of the target AST and moving downwards. During this traversal, it attempts to match namespaces, classes, or other scope-defining entities in the target AST with those found in the snippet AST. Finally, it performs a specific lookup based on the type of the snippet declaration (e.g., class, typedef, enum, or function) within the resolved target scope to find the matching symbol.

Parameters
snippet_declarationA pointer to the declaration statement in the snippet AST whose associated symbol needs to be found in the target AST.
targetScopeA pointer to the scope statement in the target AST that serves as the starting point for the reverse scope traversal.
Returns
A pointer to the SgSymbol in the target AST that corresponds to the snippet_declaration. Returns NULL if no matching symbol is found or if an unnamed enum is encountered.
Precondition
snippet_declaration must not be NULL and must be a valid SgDeclarationStatement.
targetScope must be a valid SgScopeStatement.
The scopes between the snippet_declaration and the global scope in the snippet AST must be named scopes.
Postcondition
The function returns a symbol that, if found, should have a name and declaration matching the name and type of the snippet_declaration.
Note
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the integrity of the AST traversal and the existence of symbols.
The function handles several declaration variants including V_SgClassDeclaration, V_SgTypedefDeclaration, V_SgEnumDeclaration, V_SgMemberFunctionDeclaration, and V_SgFunctionDeclaration.
Warning
The function will call ROSE_ABORT if it encounters an unexpected SgFunctionDefinition in the scope list or an unhandled declaration variant.
Unnamed enum declarations are not supported and will trigger a warning.

◆ fixupCopyOfAstFromSeparateFileInNewTargetAst() [1/2]

void SageBuilder::fixupCopyOfAstFromSeparateFileInNewTargetAst ( SgStatement * insertionPoint,

Fixes up AST nodes in a copied snippet to ensure they correctly reference the target AST's context.

This function is responsible for reconciling the differences between an original AST snippet and its copy after the copy has been inserted into a new target AST. When a snippet is copied from a separate file and inserted into a new target, its internal references (such as symbols or parent pointers) may still point to the original file's context. This function iterates through the nodes of the copied AST and applies necessary fixups to ensure that any nodes referencing elements from the original file are updated to point to the corresponding elements in the target file.

The implementation relies on the structural equivalence between the original snippet and the copy. It uses two iterators to traverse the original and the copy simultaneously, applying fixupCopyOfNodeFromSeparateFileInNewTargetAst to each node. It also temporarily enables symbol table base class searching to support Java-specific symbol resolution during the fixup process.

Parameters
insertionPointThe SgStatement representing the location in the target AST where the snippet is being inserted.
insertionPointIsScopeA boolean flag indicating whether the insertion point is a scope (e.g., a block or function body).
toInsertThe SgStatement node representing the root of the copied AST snippet that is being inserted.
original_before_copyThe SgStatement node representing the root of the original AST snippet before it was copied.
Precondition
insertionPoint must not be NULL.
toInsert must not be NULL.
original_before_copy must not be NULL.
The insertion point must belong to a valid SgFile (targetFile != NULL).
The copy (toInsert) must have already been inserted into the target AST such that its enclosing file matches the insertion point's file.
The original snippet (original_before_copy) must belong to a different SgFile than the target AST.
The AST of toInsert must be structurally equivalent to the AST of original_before_copy.
Postcondition
The nodes within the toInsert AST subtree are updated to reference the target AST's symbols and context where appropriate.
SgSymbolTable::set_force_search_of_base_classes is restored to its original state (false).
Note
This function uses ifndef USE_CMAKEx to conditionally compile the traversal logic.
If the structural equivalence check fails, the function prints a warning and returns without performing fixups.
If a mismatch in node variants is detected during traversal, the function triggers a ROSE_ABORT().

◆ getTargetFileTypeSupport()

ROSE_DLL_API SgType * SageBuilder::getTargetFileTypeSupport ( SgType * snippet_type,
SgScopeStatement * targetScope )

Analyzes and processes AST nodes for symbol re-binding and scope adjustment.

This function performs a complex re-binding of symbols when moving code snippets from one context (the source AST) to another (the target AST). It handles the following critical operations:

  • Symbol Re-binding: Updates references to classes, variables, and types so that they point to the definitions present in the target scope rather than the original source scope.
  • Scope Management: Adjusts the visibility and accessibility of symbols by updating parent/child relationships within the AST.
  • Type Resolution: Ensures that type names and class references are correctly resolved against the target's include paths and header files.
  • Namespace/Package Alignment: Handles the translation of namespaces (C++) or packages (Java) to ensure that the injected code remains semantically valid within the new compilation unit.
  • Dependency Tracking: Maintains the integrity of the symbol table by updating the links between declarations and their usages.
Parameters
nodeThe AST node currently being processed.
target_contextThe context (scope/file) into which the node is being moved.
Note
This function is highly sensitive to the integrity of the symbol table. Incorrect handling of symbol re-binding can lead to broken compilation units or incorrect type resolution during subsequent analysis phases.

Retrieves the corresponding type in the target AST that matches a given snippet type.

This function serves as an internal helper to map types from a snippet AST to their equivalent declarations and types within a target AST. It specifically handles named types (such as classes, typedefs, and enums) by locating their associated declarations in the snippet and then searching for the corresponding symbols within the provided target scope. For complex types like Java parameterized types, it attempts to resolve the underlying class symbol in the target scope.

Parameters
snippet_typeA pointer to the SgType in the snippet AST that needs to be mapped to the target AST. Must not be NULL.
targetScopeA pointer to the SgScopeStatement in the target AST where the search for the corresponding type declaration should be performed. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the corresponding SgType in the target AST if a match is found; otherwise, returns NULL if the type is not a named type or cannot be resolved.
Precondition
snippet_type != NULL
targetScope != NULL
Postcondition
If a named type is provided, the returned SgType (if not NULL) will point to a type definition existing within the targetScope's hierarchy.
Note
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate that the input parameters and intermediate lookups (like finding associated symbols) are successful.

◆ getTemplateArgumentList()

ROSE_DLL_API SgTemplateArgumentPtrList * SageBuilder::getTemplateArgumentList ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

Retrieves the list of template arguments associated with a given declaration statement.

This function inspects the variant type of the provided SgDeclarationStatement to determine if it contains template arguments. It handles various types of declarations, including template instantiations, template class declarations, template function declarations, and template member function declarations. For template instantiations, it retrieves the templateArguments field, whereas for template declarations, it retrieves the templateSpecializationArguments field. The function also accounts for non-template declarations and specific types like SgTemplateTypedefDeclaration by returning NULL or the appropriate argument list.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement whose template argument list is to be retrieved.
Returns
A pointer to an SgTemplateArgumentPtrList containing the template arguments if the declaration contains them; otherwise, returns NULL.
Precondition
decl must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The returned pointer points to the internal template argument list of the declaration if it exists, or NULL if no template arguments are present.
Note
The function uses a switch statement based on the variant type of the declaration. If the variant type falls into the default case, the function will trigger a ROSE_ABORT().

◆ initDiagnostics()

void SageBuilder::initDiagnostics ( )

Initializes the diagnostic logging system for the SageBuilder component.

This function ensures that the diagnostic logging mechanism is set up and registered exactly once during the lifetime of the application. It uses a static flag to track whether initialization has already occurred. Upon the first call, it registers the logger with the name "Rose::SageBuilder" and logs an initial comment indicating the start of the abstract syntax tree building process.

Precondition
The logging infrastructure (mlog) must be accessible within the scope of this function.
Postcondition
The diagnostic system is initialized, and subsequent calls to this function will have no effect.
Note
This function is thread-unsafe if multiple threads attempt to call it simultaneously for the first time, as the check and set of the initialized flag is not atomic.

◆ setTemplateArgumentParents()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageBuilder::setTemplateArgumentParents ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

Sets the parent nodes for template arguments within a declaration statement.

This function iterates through the list of template arguments associated with a given SgDeclarationStatement. If a template argument does not have a parent assigned, or if its current parent is a scope statement, the function updates the parent of the template argument to be the first non-defining declaration of the provided declaration statement. This ensures that the template arguments are correctly linked to the appropriate declaration context.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement whose template arguments need their parent pointers updated.
Precondition
decl must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The parent pointers of the template arguments in decl are updated to point to the first non-defining declaration of decl, provided they were either NULL or pointed to a scope statement.
Note
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate that decl is not NULL and that a non-defining declaration exists. It also utilizes ifdef ROSE_DEBUG_NEW_EDG_ROSE_CONNECTION for debug logging.

◆ setTemplateArgumentsInDeclaration()

SgTemplateArgumentPtrList * templateArgumentsList_input )

DQ (9/16/2012): Added function to support setting the template arguments and setting their parents (and for any relevant declaration).

Sets the template arguments for a specific template declaration statement.

This function updates the template argument list of a given declaration statement with the provided list of template arguments. It is designed to handle various types of template instantiations, including class, function, member function, and typedef instantiations. The function performs a deep copy of the input argument list into the existing list associated with the declaration and subsequently updates the parent pointers for the template arguments to maintain the integrity of the AST.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement that is being instantiated. The declaration must be of a template instantiation variant.
templateArgumentsList_inputA pointer to the list of template arguments to be applied to the declaration.
Precondition
templateArgumentsList_input must not be NULL.
The variant type of decl must be one of the following: V_SgTemplateInstantiationDecl, V_SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl, V_SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl, or V_SgTemplateInstantiationTypedefDeclaration.
Postcondition
If the declaration already contains a template argument list, it will be overwritten by the contents of templateArgumentsList_input.
The parent pointers of the template arguments within the declaration are updated via setTemplateArgumentParents.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the input parameters and the type of the declaration.

This function checks if the provided function declaration is a template instantiation (either a standalone function template or a member function template). If it is, the function assigns the provided name to the template name property of the instantiation. This ensures that the template name is correctly stored without template arguments, which is necessary for maintaining correct semantics during the construction of the AST.

Parameters
funcA pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration representing the function to be processed. This can be a regular function, a function template instantiation, or a member function template instantiation.

If func is identified as a template instantiation, its template name will be updated to match the provided name.
Note
This implementation handles both SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl and SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl. It relies on the logic that the input name is already stripped of template arguments to avoid complex parsing issues with nested template syntax.

ROSE_DLL_API void SageBuilder::setTemplateParameterParents ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl)

◆ testTemplateArgumentParents()

Validates that all template arguments of a declaration statement have a non-null parent.

If a template argument is found to have a null parent, an error message is printed to the standard output. The function also verifies that the declaration statement has at least one non-defining declaration.

Postcondition
The parent of every template argument in decl must be non-NULL.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to enforce structural integrity of the AST. If an assertion fails, the program will terminate.
